settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: A guard does exist on the parameter path: UaaSavedRequestAwareAuthenticationSuccessHandler lines 42-44 and UaaSavedRequestCache lines 94-97 both call UaaUrlUtils.uriHasMatchingHost against request.getServerName() before using/storing form_redirect_uri.

UaaSavedRequestCache.shouldSaveFormRedirectParameter (lines 89-103) constrains saving to POST requests with a non-empty parameter and refuses to overwrite an already-saved request, limiting some scenarios.

The "override.redirect_uri" path reads a Spring request attribute (lines 37-40), which is normally populated by server-side code rather than directly from a request parameter, so it may not be attacker-influenced in practice.
The handler appears to delegate the actual redirect behavior to the Spring/Acegi saved-request-aware base class, which was not read and may apply additional processing.
candidates.description:
UaaSavedRequestAwareAuthenticationSuccessHandler.determineTargetUrl (lines 34-47) computes the post-authentication redirect target from two untrusted-looking sources: (a) the request attribute "override.redirect_uri", which is returned verbatim with no host, scheme, or allow-list validation (lines 37-40), and (b) the request parameter "form_redirect_uri", which is returned only when UaaUrlUtils.uriHasMatchingHost(redirectFormParam, request.getServerName()) is true (lines 42-44). The (b) branch delegates all of its safety to uriHasMatchingHost; the (a) branch has no visible guard in this file.

UaaSavedRequestCache is the other half of the same flow: shouldSaveFormRedirectParameter (lines 89-103) decides whether to persist the form_redirect_uri value, gating on POST, non-empty parameter, no pre-existing saved request, and the same UaaUrlUtils.uriHasMatchingHost check (lines 94-97); saveRequest stores it inside a ClientRedirectSavedRequest (lines 82-85). ClientRedirectSavedRequest.getRedirectUrl() (lines 129-138) returns the stored redirectUrl verbatim with no further validation.

The security-relevant question is whether uriHasMatchingHost robustly rejects attacker-chosen hosts (userinfo/@-style authorities, embedded credentials, trailing-dot or suffix-partial hostnames, scheme differences, malformed authorities) and under what conditions the "override.redirect_uri" attribute can be attacker-influenced. If either source can be satisfied with an off-site origin, the login flow can be redirected to an attacker-controlled site after successful authentication (a phishing/token-leak primitive). Reported as a candidate: the primary guard (uriHasMatchingHost) and the ultimate consumer of the returned URL (the Spring saved-request redirect chain) were not read, so neither the strength of the check nor the reachability of the unguarded attribute path could be established.
missing_evidence: Full implementation of UaaUrlUtils.uriHasMatchingHost was not read; its robustness against crafted authorities (userinfo/@, embedded credentials, trailing dots, partial suffix matches, malformed hosts) is unverified.

Downstream consumption of determineTargetUrl's return value (the Spring success-handler redirect chain / SavedRequestAwareAuthenticationSuccessHandler) was not read, so absence of additional host or origin checks is unconfirmed.
Call sites that set the "override.redirect_uri" request attribute were not read, so its trust level and reachability are undetermined.
Whether form_redirect_uri can be carried into authenticated flows that bypass the POST / no-existing-saved-request conditions in shouldSaveFormRedirectParameter was not established.
ClientRedirectSavedRequest's full class (construction, serialization, equals/hashCode) beyond lines 129-138 was not read.
preconditions: A value is present for the "override.redirect_uri" request attribute, or a "form_redirect_uri" request parameter that satisfies UaaUrlUtils.uriHasMatchingHost(redirectFormParam, request.getServerName()), at the time determineTargetUrl runs.

For the form_redirect_uri path, the request must also satisfy UaaSavedRequestCache.shouldSaveFormRedirectParameter for the value to be persisted (POST request, non-empty parameter, no existing saved request) if the session-cache path rather than the attribute path carries the value.
The value reaching these code paths is influenced by an attacker (e.g. a crafted login form submission or a crafted saved request) rather than being exclusively server-generated.
candidates.title: Unvalidated redirect target from "override.redirect_uri" request attribute, and host-check-gated form_redirect_uri, in UaaSavedRequestAwareAuthenticationSuccessHandler / UaaSavedRequestCache
